title: Approve a sarcopenia drug that improves strength and physical function

concept.text: Treat age-related sarcopenia with a medicine that improves patients' functional ability, rather than muscle mass alone. Bimagrumab increased lean mass in a randomized trial but did not significantly improve its primary physical-performance endpoint. Proposed completion test: FDA or EMA approval specifically for sarcopenia, following a pivotal randomized trial in consensus-defined patients showing a clinically meaningful improvement in strength and mobility or disability over at least 12 months. Test set by: Regulators would set approval requirements. EWGSOP2 supplies a diagnostic framework emphasizing low strength, confirmation by low muscle quantity/quality, and physical performance for severity; the 12-month duration is editorial. Overlaps: ORT-06, PHA-09, LON-03. Sources given: [EWGSOP2 consensus definition](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/mid/EMS80409/) ; [Randomized bimagrumab trial in sarcopenia](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2771858).

page.title: Pharmacotherapy for age-related sarcopenia
page.definition: A medicine approved to treat age-related sarcopenia provides clinical benefit in physical function. Sarcopenia is a muscle disorder identified by low strength and confirmed by reduced muscle quantity or quality.

goal.need: In a randomized trial of 180 adults aged at least 70 years, bimagrumab increased lean body mass but did not significantly improve the primary physical-performance endpoint. Participants received nutritional support and exercise in both groups. The results establish why increasing muscle mass alone cannot demonstrate the functional benefit sought from a sarcopenia medicine.

figures.caption: Changes after six months in the randomized bimagrumab trial
figures.note: Bimagrumab 700 mg monthly: 113 participants; placebo: 67. Values are mean changes. The performance battery assesses balance, walking and chair rises.

statements.body: European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2
statements.quote: EWGSOP2 emphasizes that practitioners have ever-increasing possibilities for preventing, delaying, treating, and sometimes even reversing sarcopenia by way of early and effective interventions.
Muscle weakness is a risk factor for falls
statements.context: FDA's patient-focused drug-development meeting for sarcopenia on 6 April 2017.

statements.quote: During the first half of 2026, Biophytis continued the development of BIO101 (20-hydroxyecdysone), primarily for the sarcopenia and obesity indications.

completion.title: FDA approves a medicine to treat age-related sarcopenia on evidence of functional benefit.
completion.criterion: FDA issues marketing approval and prescribing information explicitly indicating a medicine for treating age-related sarcopenia, with clinical benefit in patients' physical function supporting the indication. FDA determines that the medicine is safe and effective for this intended use. The approval letter and prescribing information provide the verification record.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, general marketing-approval standard described in Step 4: FDA Drug Review; no sarcopenia-specific numerical approval standard was located.
completion.threshold_quote: safe and effective for its intended use
completion.basis: Indication-specific marketing approval supplies an externally adjudicated completion test. ESCEO recommends physical performance and a patient-reported outcome as phase III co-primary endpoints, with strength as a secondary endpoint. Its 12-month recommendation is a society recommendation, not an identified FDA requirement.

milestones.title: A sarcopenia candidate demonstrates pharmacological activity in laboratory studies.
milestones.criterion: Preclinical studies establish pharmacological activity warranting clinical development under FDA's framework; safety must also be evaluated before human exposure. In research first published on 8 December 2023, BIO101 at 50 mg/kg/day for 14 weeks increased maximum treadmill speed to 0.515 ± 0.02 m/s in 10 old female mice versus 0.44 ± 0.02 m/s in 8 vehicle-treated old mice, with P < 0.05. Both groups received a high-fat diet. This establishes animal efficacy, not completion of a regulatory toxicology package.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, preclinical pharmacological-activity criterion; this is a general development criterion, not a sarcopenia-specific effect-size threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: if the compound exhibits pharmacological activity that justifies commercial development.

milestones.title: A sarcopenia candidate completes phase I testing without unacceptable toxicity.
milestones.criterion: Human exposure establishes tolerability and dosing sufficient to proceed beyond phase I, applying FDA's stated toxicity gate. A bimagrumab phase I report first published on 17 December 2022 included 91 randomized healthy adults aged at least 70 years; 84 completed the study. Participants received intravenous or subcutaneous regimens and were followed through week 20. The investigators reported that adverse events were mostly mild or moderate. These participants did not constitute a sarcopenia efficacy population.
milestones.set_by: FDA, The FDA's Drug Review Process: Ensuring Drugs Are Safe and Effective, transition from phase I to phase II.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 2 studies begin if Phase 1 studies don't reveal unacceptable toxicity.

milestones.title: A sarcopenia drug improves 400-m walking speed by at least 0.10 m/s over placebo after 26 weeks.
milestones.criterion: Meet SARA-INT's sponsor-published target: a between-group difference of at least 0.10 m/s in change in 400-m walking speed after 26 weeks. This is programme-specific. The report published on 3 March 2025 randomized 233 participants aged at least 65 years. Its primary analysis combined six- and nine-month assessments: BIO101 350 mg twice daily improved speed by 0.07 m/s versus placebo in the full analysis set of 232 participants, without statistical significance. The per-protocol estimate in 156 participants was 0.09 m/s, P = 0.008. Neither estimate reached the stated magnitude.
milestones.set_by: Biophytis, SARA-INT trial NCT03452488, primary-endpoint target disclosed in its Form 20-F for the financial year ended 31 December 2023.
milestones.threshold_quote: A minimum clinically significant benefit is set at 0.10 meter per second in the mean difference between groups.

milestones.title: A 12-month phase III sarcopenia drug trial meets physical-performance and patient-reported co-primary endpoints.
milestones.criterion: A randomized, double-blind trial against placebo plus standard care meets its prespecified co-primary efficacy criteria for physical performance and a patient-reported outcome, with at least 12 months of treatment and follow-up. ESCEO recommends ambulatory adults aged at least 70 years with low strength and low physical performance, and inability to complete the 400-m walk as the performance endpoint. It supplies no universal treatment-effect margin. Biophytis' report dated 30 October 2026 described SARA-31 phase III preparations; trial initiation remained conditional on partnerships and funding.
milestones.set_by: European Society for Clinical and Economic Aspects of Osteoporosis, Osteoarthritis and Musculoskeletal Diseases, 2020 update of its sarcopenia drug-trial recommendations; these are society recommendations.
milestones.threshold_quote: co-primary endpoints, combining a measure of physical performance with a Patient Reported Outcome Measure (PROM).

not_found: Searches of FDA and EMA guidance and approval pages found no sarcopenia-specific numerical efficacy threshold for marketing approval.
No published regulatory requirement for both strength and physical function as sarcopenia co-primary endpoints was located.
No successful phase III sarcopenia drug trial meeting the ESCEO co-primary framework was located.
The ClinicalTrials.gov page for NCT02333331 did not expose its study fields; the published bimagrumab trial was accessible.

results.finding: BIO101-treated old female mice (n=10) reached a maximum treadmill speed of 0.515 ± 0.02 m/s.
results.detail: After 14 weeks at 50 mg/kg/day on a high-fat diet, speed was higher than in vehicle-treated old mice (n=8; 0.44 ± 0.02 m/s; P < 0.05). The figure legend lists different group sizes. This demonstrates animal efficacy, not completion of a regulatory toxicology package.
results.quote: BIO101 treatment of old animals increased the maximal running speed (0.515 ± 0.02 m/s) compared with vehicle‐treated (+17%,  P  < 0.05) and significantly compensated the loss of running velocity (Figure  5C ).

results.finding: MF-300 increased maximal muscle force by 20% in aged mice; sample size not reported.
results.detail: Male aged mice received oral MF-300 for 12 weeks. This is an unpublished preclinical result for a different candidate; it does not report the specified BIO101 experiment or establish completion of a regulatory toxicology package.

results.finding: Bimagrumab phase I: 84 of 91 randomized healthy older adults completed the study.
results.detail: Bimagrumab was generally well tolerated, with adverse events mostly mild or moderate; the authors considered the subcutaneous route feasible for future clinical development. Participants were not a sarcopenia efficacy population.

results.finding: BIO101 phase I study in 54 healthy adults reported zero serious adverse events.
results.detail: The study completed in December 2016. All treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate; 350 mg twice daily was selected for the sarcopenia phase II study. Participants were healthy volunteers.
results.quote: No deaths, SAEs or treatment emergent AEs (TEAEs) leading to treatment discontinuation were reported during the study. All TEAEs were mild or moderate in severity

results.finding: MF-300 phase I enrolled 88 adults; no serious adverse events were reported.
results.detail: Single doses up to 800 mg and repeat doses up to 200 mg daily were well tolerated. The investigators reported that the data support continued development and planned a phase 2b study.
results.quote: • No deaths, serious adverse events, or discontinuations due to adverse events

results.finding: BIO101: in a 156-person per-protocol population, the observed 400-m walking-speed difference versus placebo at month 6 was 0.102 m/s.
results.detail: The observed month-6 estimate meets the magnitude threshold. The number with observed data is not stated. The reported primary analysis combined months 6 and 9 and estimated 0.09 m/s in the per-protocol population; 55% of end-of-treatment on-site assessments were lost.
results.quote: In the PP population, the observed difference between treatment arms and placebo was −0.019 and 0.102 m/s for 175 and 350 mg BIO101, respectively, at M6 and 0.019 and 0.078 m/s for 175 and 350 mg BIO101, respectively, at M6/M9 (Figure  S1 ).
